clue.text: Run in election, Attorney-General having been rejected

indicators.note: rejected is taken as thrown back, so the combined letters are read from right to left

parts.note: a poll is a vote or election

explanation.surface: A politician standing for office after the government's chief law officer has been turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having been rejected' turns POLLAG round, the poll followed by AG.
explanation.definitionFit: To run fast, as a horse does at full speed, is a synonym of the answer as a verb.

clue.text: Give weapons to others in support

parts.note: to arm someone is to give them weapons
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: Supplying arms to other nations to back them up.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded rest for a limb on a chair is a physical support for the elbow.

clue.text: Fast bowler's second is slow

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting before Easter

indicators.note: the second of a word is its second letter

explanation.surface: A cricket paradox: the fast bowler's second delivery is slow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' suggests a cricketer's pace but is the Lenten fast; the second letter of 'bowler's' is O.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning to play at a slow tempo.

clue.text: Bread wrapper taken from work?

parts.note: bread is slang for money, so the wrapper is the envelope holding wages brought home from the job

explanation.surface: Someone bringing home packaging from a loaf at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money, not a loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: The envelope in which weekly wages in cash were handed to workers.

clue.text: Independent group following worker's protection against infection

indicators.note: following places the independent group after the worker in the assembled word

parts.note: a worker is an ant, the classic crossword worker insect
a body is an organised group, as in a governing body

explanation.surface: A trade union picture: an independent body backing a worker's protection, made to sound medical.
explanation.definitionFit: The immune system makes these proteins to neutralise invading germs, so they protect the body from disease.

clue.text: Dress is concerning, held in disgust

indicators.note: held in means contained inside, so the concerning word sits within the disgust word

parts.note: to appal is to horrify or disgust
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A frock is regarded with distaste by some fashion critic.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing in general, a formal synonym for dress as a noun.

clue.text: Label covering new and old dance music

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the label word encloses the new letter

parts.note: a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A record label releasing fresh and vintage dance tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: An Argentine ballroom dance, and the music written for it, so an example.

clue.text: Engineers employed by poor business may be on this, financially

indicators.note: employed by means working within, so the engineers sit inside the poor business

parts.note: a bad line is an unprofitable line of business
RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers working for a failing firm may end up on the poverty threshold.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as the definition; the definition proper is the closing phrase, with 'poor business' as BAD LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on this means living at subsistence level, so in poverty; the phrase describes where the poor may be.

clue.text: Smart dogs regularly fed with a cut of beef

indicators.note: fed with means given something inside, so the dog letters take in the rest
regularly takes every other letter, here the first and third

parts.note: shin is a cut of beef from the lower leg

explanation.surface: Fashionable dogs dined routinely on a piece of beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dogs regularly' gives D and G, which take in A plus SHIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylish and elegant in appearance, a synonym of smart in the dress sense.

clue.text: Sadly many pensioners will have no answer for sources of income

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone awry, so the remaining letters are rearranged
says the fodder must lose the letter that follows

explanation.surface: A lament that many retirees will get no reply about where their money comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will have no' removes the A of 'answer' from MANY PENSIONERS before 'Sadly' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Profitable ventures that bring in plenty of cash are described by this phrase.

clue.text: Sophisticated girl coming out on song

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young woman making her entrance into society
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A sophisticated young woman makes her society debut to music.
explanation.walkthrough: A debutante 'comes out' into society, an old upper-class British custom.
explanation.definitionFit: A suave, urbane and stylishly confident person is described by this word, a near synonym.

clue.text: Contents of wordy article printed by popular decree

indicators.note: the contents are what lies inside, so the outer letters of the word are dropped

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A long-winded piece published by popular demand.
explanation.definitionFit: To decree something is to order it officially, which is a synonym of the answer as a verb.

clue.text: Hit, and unable to move across river

indicators.note: across means spanning, so the word for unable to move lies around the river letter

parts.note: stuck means fixed in place, unable to move

explanation.surface: Someone struck and stranded on the far side of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of the verb meaning to strike, so hit in the sense of having delivered a blow.

clue.text: Slip perhaps reporting to battle full of energy

parts.note: working under someone means reporting to them

indicators.note: full of means containing, so the battle word holds the energy letter

parts.note: war is battle or conflict
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A soldier answering to command marches off to battle, brimming with vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip' looks like a mistake but is the garment; 'reporting' suggests a sound effect but means answering to.
explanation.definitionFit: A petticoat slip is an example of intimate garments, hence the hint perhaps.

clue.text: End of promotions should come after flogging lots

indicators.note: places the flogging word first with the final letter tacked on behind it

parts.note: lashing is whipping or flogging

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A grim piece of naval discipline: after the promotions come floggings in abundance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of promotions' is S, which comes after LASHING.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal British word for a generous quantity, as in cream poured on in abundance.

clue.text: Station crowd gets breaking news

parts.note: a stop is a station on a route
a press is a crowd or throng

explanation.surface: Journalists swarm a railway station over an unfolding story.
explanation.definitionFit: Late news inserted into a newspaper after printing has started, so the latest bulletin.

clue.text: Managing director reveals someone owed a debt

indicators.note: managing means handling or arranging, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A company boss is exposed as the one the firm owes money to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Managing director' looks like a single job title, but 'Managing' is the anagram signal working on 'director'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lender or supplier who is due repayment is the standard term for a person or firm owed money.

clue.text: Strangely asleep after run, showing setback to recovery

indicators.note: after puts the jumbled letters behind the run letter

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: strangely says the letters are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: A jogger oddly dozing off after a run, which slows their convalescence.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling back into illness after improving is a setback in recovery.

clue.text: Wine resurrected in Lancashire?

parts.note: red is red wine
Christ rose from the dead, so resurrected means rose

explanation.surface: Wine revived in a north-west English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire is a county in north-west England whose emblem is a red flower; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: This flower is the heraldic emblem of Lancashire, so it stands for the county.

clue.text: Oxygen's needed by fool grabbing tail of savage cat

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing, so the fool word holds the letter that follows

parts.note: clot is British slang for a fool

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A fool needs air when seized by the tail of a ferocious cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail of savage' is E, which CLOT grabs to make CELOT after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: A spotted wild feline of the Americas, so an example of the wider category.

clue.text: Too full of themselves at first, for all to see

indicators.note: full of means containing, so the too word holds the first letter

parts.note: overly means too, excessively

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: People too self-important at first, showing it openly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Too full of themselves' reads as a phrase about conceit, but 'full of' puts T inside OVERLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Done openly and visibly, so the adverb means publicly, in plain view.

clue.text: Irish county town's beginning to make wine?

parts.note: Clare is a county on Ireland's west coast

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A small Irish town starting to produce its own wine, offered with a doubtful question mark.
explanation.walkthrough: Clare is a county in western Ireland. The question mark flags that the definition is an example, a red Bordeaux.
explanation.definitionFit: The British name for red Bordeaux wine, so an example of the general term.

clue.text: Health e-tailers must enclose letter

indicators.note: the words given must enclose the answer, which sits inside them across the word break

explanation.surface: Online health shops are required to include a letter with their parcels.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, so an example of a letter.

clue.text: Left section in action

indicators.note: in places the section word inside the action word

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
a part is a section of something

explanation.surface: A unit of troops left behind while in combat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has gone away or set off has left, a synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Chap that's understood?

definitions.meaning: a man's name, so any fellow
the radio word confirming a message was received and understood

explanation.surface: A man checking that he has been understood.
explanation.definitionFit: A common man's name and the radio procedure word for message received.

clue.text: Coins once found by men on board belonging to crew

parts.note: chessmen on a board are called pieces
of expresses belonging, as in friend of mine
an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: Old coins discovered by sailors aboard ship and belonging to the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'men on board' suggests sailors but means chessmen; an eight is a rowing crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Spanish silver dollars worth eight reales, famous from pirate tales, so historical currency.

clue.text: Cut down on relaxation after December — right?

indicators.note: after puts the relaxation word behind the month abbreviation

parts.note: ease is rest or relaxation

explanation.surface: A resolution to relax less after the December holidays, posed as a question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut down on relaxation' looks like the definition, but the definition stops at 'Cut down'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce or lessen something is to cut it down, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Speaks about system of voting for wets

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the speaking word goes round the voting letters

parts.note: says means speaks
PR stands for proportional representation, an electoral system

explanation.surface: Someone holding forth on electoral reform for the benefit of political moderates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wets' looks like a noun, Tory moderates in British slang, but it is the verb: makes damp.
explanation.definitionFit: To shower liquid over something is to dampen it, a synonym in the present tense.
